statement: Fix a window system W for a finite grid L, and either bracket from Lemma 7.1. Let K0, . . . , Kq ⋐ D be disks, with K0 at positive distance from every Kj, j ≥ 1, and let Xδ, Fδ be as in (7.1). Suppose there are two levels ℓ− < ℓ+ in L such that: (i) K0 is strictly between the two levels, and both levels avoid every spectator disk Kj with positive margin; (ii) after opening sufficiently small gaps inside their corresponding windows, every pin arc and spectator disk in the middle band belongs to one of the two strictly separated u-projection families in (7.12). Then lim δ↓0 Eµ±,W δ [Hδ(∆ϕ)Fδ] = 0. (7.19) In particular it applies to products of bounded continuous functions of finitely many smooth zero- total tests in each Kj. There is no disjointness requirement between spectator disks. For this latter class the identity passes to any subsequential distributional limit of the bracket laws. For any fixed bound q on the number of spectator disks these geometric hypotheses can be ar- ranged locally as follows. Fix x ∈ D and ρ > 0 with B(x, ρ) ⊂ D. Take K0 sufficiently small about x, and take at most q spectator disks of sufficiently small radii, all outside B(x, ρ). From a sufficiently dense grid of regular levels one can choose the two levels within a fixed small fraction of ρ above and below x. The choices and smallness bounds depend on q and ρ, not on the number of terms in a later linear combination of such products.
